assessment: The authors study insulin secretion in acutely prepared pancreatic slices and find that it is remarkably different from what is observed in isolated islets. In particular, the work shows that polar differentiation and higher stimulus-secretion coupling is caused by integrin-mediated and local establishment of effective release sites where the beta cells contact the capillaries, involving concentration of active zone proteins and clustering of calcium channels. The findings are important and should be of significant interest to the part of readership with an interest in the regulation of exocytosis in general and insulin secretion in particular.
